item.title: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty
item.description: NBC Sports analyst and former Cincinnati Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth blasted defensive back Jordan Battle for his taunting penalty during the second quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' loss to Jacksonville because of a hamstring injury. Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. He played in all 51 of the Bengals' games over his first three seasons, recording six interceptions and making 30 starts. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of the Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss . Battle was injured during the fourth quarter of the Bengals' Week 13 loss to Pittsburgh last season. During the 2024 season, Battle recovered a fumble and returned it during the third quarter of the Bengals' NFL Week 15 win against Tennessee, but Battle lost the ball just shy of the goal line through the back of the end zone for a touchback. Play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico missed the Week 9 Sunday night game between the Bucs and Bears in Chicago because of a health issue . Noah Eagle called the Bucs-Bears game with Collinsworth and sideline reporter Melissa Stark. NBC Sports analyst Devin McCourty said during the week that he was eager to see the reception for former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin at Paycor Stadium. "I'm excited to see if Mike Tomlin gets booed this week, if people hate him, or are throwing things at him," McCourty told reporters Nov. 11. In 2024, Tirico referred to the tackle then- Bengals linebacker Logan Wilson made in 2023 of Ravens tight end Mark Andrews as a "hip-drop tackle." In an exclusive Q&A in 2022 with The Enquirer, Tirico talked about working with Collinsworth, why the Wild Card Playoff win against the Las Vegas Raiders was the most memorable Bengals game he's called, and his long-time friendship with Bengals radio play-by-play announcer Dan Hoard. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty

item.title: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final
item.description: Another deep tournament run ended in unfortunately familiar fashion for the St. Charles soccer team. The Cardinals almost tripled Kettering Fairmont in shots and earned a handful of quality scoring chances in the Division I boys state final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, but the first-time state finalist Firebirds converted a higher percentage of opportunities and came away with a 3-1 win. Senior forward Sam Lofthouse scored St. Charles’ only goal, spinning and shooting from about 25 yards to the right of the goal with 25:35 to play and sneaking his shot into the upper right corner. That made it 2-1, but Fairmont (15-5-3) got the goal back less than four minutes later. Gavin Weaver’s corner kick got all the way through traffic, and Luke Davidson put it in from right in front. Azariyah Nsabimama and Aaron Black scored 12 minutes apart in the first half for Fairmont, and St. Charles lost for only the fourth time this season (18-4-1) and first since its regular-season finale Oct. 15 against Worthington Kilbourne. St. Charles, appearing in its 12th state tournament, fourth in a row and seeking its first title since 1985, outshot Fairmont 23-8. The Cardinals also were state runners-up in 2024, 2016, 1991, 1988 and 1981. St. Charles had outscored its first five tournament opponents 15-3, including a 1-0 win over defending state champion Dublin Jerome in a state semifinal in which Lofthouse had the only goal. Cardinals sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves. Fairmont’s Carson Dewald stopped six shots. This story will be updated. item.title: Jayson Tatum offers honest Cooper Flagg outlook after Celtics blast Mavericks
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Jayson Tatum offers honest Cooper Flagg outlook after Celtics blast Mavericks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics have exceeded expectations with their 11-2 start to the current NBA season. Their latest victory was a 131-94 triumph over the Dallas Mavericks and that game allowed the Celtics to move into first place in the Atlantic Division. The Celtics have a one-half game lead over the Philadelphia 76ers. Most expected the Celtics to lose some of their luster after trading superstar Jaylen Brown to the Sixers and installing veteran Paul George into the lineup. Instead, George has been healthy and has been a solid fit in head coach Joe Mazzulla’s rotation. The win over the Mavericks saw the Celtics build a 42-9 lead at the conclusion of the first quarter. That was Boston’s largest lead at the end of the opening quarter in team history. It was the best performance of an NBA team in the first quarter since the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in 1987. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Celtics were led by Jayson Tatum , who scored 32 points and added 6 rebounds and 6 assists. He made 11 of 18 field goal attempts, and he was successful on 5 of 8 3-point attempts. Derrick White supplemented Tatum’s production with 16 points and 4 rebounds. Second-year star Cooper Flagg had 17 points for the Mavericks (7-7), and he caught Tatum’s eye with his showing. “I think what he’s done thus far in the league has been incredible,” Tatum said , per Celtics beat reporter Daniel Donabedian. “So it’s going to be fun to watch him as his career continues to grow. “As he gets older, the game is just going to continue to slow down (for him).”

item.title: 'You live for them, you play for them' - Auston Trusty honors late father with goal on emotional USMNT return
item.description: Auston Trusty GFX - GOAL In his first match since his father’s death, Auston Trusty scored against Haiti and found comfort in the teammates he calls family. The goal was only part of the story. MIAMI -- For one brief moment, Auston Trusty's sadness subsided, and his competitiveness took over. As he ran towards the corner flag after scoring his second U.S. Men's National Team goal, Trusty got caught up in the moment. He cupped his hands and stared at the crowd full of Haitian fans just seconds after giving his side a 1-0 lead. And then, as he ran back to his spot on the field, he remembered. The goal faded and reality set in. As happy as he was with his finish, Trusty was still adjusting to a new reality, one without the man he looked up to most. Saturday’s game was Trusty’s first since his father, Walt, passed away on Oct. 19. The weeks since have been difficult, to say the least. Celtic granted him time away to grieve, and he joined USMNT camp directly after attending his father’s funeral. Saturday marked his return to competitive action. It was fitting, then, that Trusty was the first USMNT player to find a moment of joy against Haiti. It didn't fix anything, and it won't, but Trusty's early goal brought peace and comfort to a man who has spent the last few weeks searching for just that. "I'm just honored to represent him," Trusty said postgame, "and play with his last name and showcase for him. I want to showcase to the world what I can do for him and his glory. I'm just very proud to score today and have a good game." Even in a 6-0 win where goals blend, Trusty's goal stood out. It was, as he said, a tribute to something bigger. More specifically, it was a tribute to someone who meant so much to him. A difficult time Unless you’ve experienced it, it’s hard to grasp the emotional toll of losing a parent. Trusty has spent the past few weeks grappling with that loss alongside his family in Pennsylvania. Walt Trusty, like his son, was a standout athlete. Back home in Media, Pa., he was a history-making basketball player in the late 60s and early 70s. As his playing days ended, his fandom remained, as he supported the local Philadelphia teams. More importantly, he also supported his children. He had six of them, and Auston was his youngest. As Trusty blossomed as a soccer star, first locally and then in Europe, the centerback's father was there every step of the way. Just this summer, he was able to watch on as his son played in, and scored in, a World Cup. "The past few weeks have been very, very tough," Trusty said on Saturday, reflecting on his father's impact on his life. "Probably the toughest of my life. Losing my father, it's never easy losing a parent, but you live for them, you play for them. He was very influential for me growing up, and also put me in the position I'm in today." More importantly, he also supported his children. He had six of them, and Auston was his youngest. As Trusty blossomed as a soccer star, first locally and then in Europe, the centerback's father was there every step of the way. Just this summer, he was able to watch on as his son played in, and scored in, a World Cup. "The past few weeks have been very, very tough," Trusty said on Saturday, reflecting on his father's impact on his life. "Probably the toughest of my life. Losing my father, it's never easy losing a parent, but you live for them, you play for them. He was very influential for me growing up, and also put me in the position I'm in today." On Saturday, Trusty was named to the starting XI for the USMNT. It was his first game since Oct. 15, four days before his father's passing. It didn't take long for Trusty to make an impact, either, despite all he'd been through. A fitting tribute Trusty got everything right as he scored a memorable goal, although the celebration didn't quite go to plan. The defender played all 90 minutes in the USMNT's 6-0 win. It was the first goal that was the most important, though, in more ways than one. In the 10th minute, the USMNT earned a free kick a few yards outside of the box. Sebastian Berhalter stepped up to hit it. The midfielder's free kick went over the Haiti defense and right onto the foot of Trusty. The defender made no mistake, placing his shot into the back of the net first-time. The emotion came over him, but not in the way he expected. "I thought before the game, 'Okay, if I score, I'll do this'," he said. "I don't know what happened, but I did the good old [hand cupping] just because it's the beginning of the game, they're loud, and they had a chance, and they thought they had something. So just me being competitive, I did that. "Then after, when I was running back, I said, 'Dang, why didn't I do something?' Next goal...To score that goal and also to have the win today. It really meant a lot." Celebration or no celebration, by the end of the match, Trusty had come to terms with the moment. He knew what it represented, both for himself and for his grieving family. It also meant something to his found family, too, as they've supported him through his tough time. The USMNT family Trusty is surrounded by familiar faces when he joins the USMNT The USMNT are filled with people Trusty has known for most of his life. He met Mark McKenzie and Matt Freese as kids coming up with the Philadelphia Union. There are 11 players in the current squad that he battled alongside this summer during the World Cup. In that sense, the national team is a second family, one that has been there for some of Trusty's best and worst moments. This month is undeniably one of the worst and, in that moment, Trusty says the USMNT have stepped up. That's what families do, after all. "These guys in my family," he said. "I've known them for a very long time, from the staff to the players, so it's just coming into a nice, warm environment that's very welcoming and very understanding of the situation. "They're all my brothers, so if I'm hurting inside, they're hurting as well. I'm really happy to come back here as my first stop." 'It means a lot' Saturday's gameball will be among the most heartfelt mementos Trusty receives during his career. After the match, the USMNT gathered in the locker room. Captain Tyler Adams stepped up, holding the game ball. "Trusty, there are some things bigger than soccer, man," he said in a moment showcased by the USMNT's social media. "The way that you played tonight, obviously getting a goal, it just means a lot. The federation is obviously behind you, the team is behind you. I just want to recognize you with this, man." Trusty stepped up, composed, and grabbed a game ball that will feel different than any he'd received before. This wasn't just commemorating a goal; it was, in a way, commemorating a person and a lifetime. "Thank you. It means a lot," a visibly emotional Trusty said. "Obviously it's not easy losing your father, but to come here and represent the country, represent all you guys, it really means a lot to me." "I don't want to cry," he added, fighting back tears," but thank you, guys, very much, and I appreciate it." Trusty may have forgotten the celebration he had planned, but Saturday’s game will be one he never forgets. It was his first match since losing his father, a first step forward through a grief still fresh. There will be more moments in a USMNT shirt, and more moments with that Trusty name on the back. Maybe next time, he’ll remember the celebration. On Saturday, though, he didn’t need one to make it clear who he was playing for.

The Chiefs have a brutal stretch from Week 12-16, which includes matchups against the Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Bengals, Patriots, and San Francisco 49ers. Three of those five games will be on the road. As for the Broncos, just two of their remaining eight games are against teams that currently have a winning record — the Steelers in Week 12, and the Bills in Week 16. The rest of their opponents include the Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Patriots, Raiders, and Chargers. The Chiefs will conclude the season with a road game against the Chargers in Week 17, and a home matchup against the Raiders in Week 18. Depending on how well they survive the stretch that proceeds that, those could be must-win games. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Are Chiefs Leading the AFC West? Overall, for his first start, I thought it was a good start.” The Raiders decided to use one of George Allen’s lines in proclaiming the Mendoza Era — “The Future Is Now” — and that’s all well and good. He was going to debut as the team’s starter at some point so why not attach a tag to it? These days, it seems it’s all in the marketing and social media details. Mendoza received a huge ovation from the crowd of 62,624 when he as introduced with the offensive starters prior to kickoff. It must have been quite a rush for him. And when he capped the first drive as a starter with a 10-yard TD run, well, elation probably doesn’t quite cover what he felt. Was he perfect? Not quite. The Seahawks were determined to not let him dominate. They sacked him six times and harassed him plenty, which is what the Legion of Boom does to opposing quarterbacks. But he also displayed great poise and confidence, at least in the first half as he helped lead the Raiders to a 10-7 halftime lead. He kept drives going which greatly helped the Raiders’ defense get sufficient rest. And credit Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko for their game plan and play-calling. They didn’t put Mendoza in a lot of high-risk situations where he could fail. He completed his first seven passes and looked like he had a command of the offense. The second half? Mendoza and the Raiders struggled mightily. Five straight drives of three-and-out for minus-17 yards in total offense before getting untracked sort of late in the game. Once the Raiders fell behind and started chasing the game, that cautious play-calling went out the window. Yes, the Raiders still continue to struggle in running the ball effectively. They managed just 65 yards on the ground. And when they lost Bowers to an ankle injury, there went one of Mendoza’s top targets. But Mendoza showed an ability to adjust. One good thing about being a second-string quarterback, you get to work with second-string receivers in practice every day. So he had a familiarity with Jack Bech and Cody White and he got the ball to both of them for first downs during the second quarter. Now that he’s the QB1, Mendoza will hopefully find a comfort zone with Michael Mayer, Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor along with Bowers. Still, the same problems that plagued the Silver and Black when Cousins was the starting quarterback were in play with Mendoza at the controls. The offensive line failed to hold up. The run game was stagnant. And when Mendoza had time, which wasn’t often, he was unable to connect downfield with his receivers. For Mendoza, there’ll certainly be better days. But when your line doesn’t block for you and you’re unable to run the ball and teams are pressuring you into being uncomfortable, what are you supposed to do? Throw in the fact the Seahawks were able to move the ball as Drew Lock and Jaxon Smith-Njigba did plenty of damage together and it was a story we’ve seen numerous times this year. JSN caught eight passes for 171 yards, including a 71-yard TD in the third quarter as Seattle took control of the game. So we’ll see what happens a week from now in Denver. Mendoza will undoubtedly learn from the experience. He certainly learned that life as a rookie starting quarterback in the NFL is no picnic. “It’s good to get punched in the face, because now it’s a great opportunity to grow and learn and unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future hopeful leader of this offense,”Mendoza said. Kubiak was more succinct. “We have to play better,” he said “We got to support (Mendoza) better.” Yes and yes.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jaden McDaniels had been enjoying a different view of the Timberwolves’ defense. With Jaylen Clark taking on more responsibility against opposing guards, McDaniels could spend additional possessions surveying the floor, calling out screens and helping teammates. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday’s loss to Chicago and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, according to Jace Frederick of the Pioneer Press . He left the game after just three minutes. The evaluation is a checkpoint rather than a confirmed return date. item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic gives ‘amazing player’ his flowers after torching Suns
item.description: Danielle Cortez-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic gives ‘amazing player’ his flowers after torching Suns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers rolled to their eighth straight win after beating the Phoenix Suns, 131-123 , at PHX Arena on Sunday, with Luka Doncic delivering another masterful performance. Doncic exploded for 43 points on 13-of-28 shooting, including 5-of-13 from long distance. He added three rebounds and nine assists. The Lakers improved to 12-2, tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the Western Conference. With Austin Reaves sidelined by a heel injury , Quentin Grimes filled the void with 22 points on 7-of-10 shooting, including 5-of-6 from rainbow territory, six rebounds, and two steals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Doncic saluted Grimes for stepping up , as reported by Lakers Today’s Raj Chipalu. “He’s becoming himself again. We really need that. He’s an amazing player. He’s going to help us a lot, and tonight he showed what kind of player he is,” said the six-time All-Star. The Lakers acquired Grimes in the offseason, signing him to a four-year, $60 million contract. The team envisioned him as a perfect fit alongside Doncic and Reaves with his two-way acumen. Grimes, however, has been struggling with consistency. Before the game against the Suns, he was averaging 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.5 assists. If Reaves continues to miss time, the 26-year-old Grimes will get more opportunities. He has shown he can produce on both ends, and Doncic’s vote of confidence should bode well for him. Grimes may have found a home with the Lakers after playing for four teams—the New York Knicks, the Detroit Pistons, the Dallas Mavericks, and the Philadelphia 76ers—in five years. item.description: Here's everything Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud said following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 10, including his thoughts on the Texans' outlook beyond Sunday's loss. Question: What do you feel like changed the most there from the first half to the second half? C.J. Stroud: “They just started pressuring and getting sticky in coverage. We really didn’t adjust to it. We gotta do a better job coming out in the second half and finding ways to move the ball and get points.” Q: The momentum shift- did you guys kinda feel like, “we had it.” And then it starts to slip away? Stroud: “That’s football. It’s a four-quarter game. They’ve come back on a lot of teams this season and won a lot of games with two-minute drives. We knew what it was. We were just dead. We gotta find a way to execute and create more energy on the sideline and keep things going." Q: DeMeco [Ryans] was talking about the penalty issue. It’ll get better, and then it keeps coming up. As a team leader, what do you see from your perspective on the penalties? Stroud: “We gotta play better as players. There’s a lot of things where we don’t need the penalty. We’ll take if you get beat just let the guy go on special teams, or the false starts, we gotta fix that. I don’t know all the other penalties we had but those are the main ones that I thought affected the game. I have the utmost hope and faith in Tae [Ersery] and whatever happened on special teams, the guys getting it fixed. The time is now. We gotta be moreurgent because time is running out.” Q: What made it difficult for you guys to adjust to some of the pressure and them being stickier in coverage? Stroud: “Honestly I don’t know. We gotta find ways to protect it, because guys are open on the back end. That’s what I think a lot of teams will do. They’ll just pressure and try to say, ‘you gotta make a big play.’ I think we gotta be able to not just run two to three routes, widen our route tree, and just run by people sometimes, and do it more often. While owner Jerry Jones was hoping to see the Dallas Cowboys upset the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, it didn’t end up happening, as the franchise experienced another disappointing loss to the NFC foe in a shootout, 46-40. There’s no question, you pay a price when you’re doing it for the first time. … I still like [our] bet [on him],” Jones said, via Jon Machota. At any rate, it remains to be seen if the Cowboys change their mind on Schottenheimer, as the head coach looks to bounce back next Sunday against the Tennessee Titans with a 4-6 record, putting them second in the NFC East. item.title: 'When the moment was big, he was at his best': Mike Tirico pays touching tribute to Dan Hicks
item.description: Credit: NBC Legendary sportscaster Dan Hicks died unexpectedly last week at the age of 64. Since the moment the news broke, those that worked with Hicks have been issuing remembrances of their colleague and offering condolences to those he left behind. Mike Tirico added his own tribute to the list on Sunday Night Football , and had nothing but the highest praise for Hicks. Of his style on the microphone, Tirico said Hicks was “No schtick. All substance,” and constantly making those around him better. “It’s no coincidence that some of the best sports analysts ever shined next to Hicksy,” Tirico said in a tribute package. “Meticulously prepared. A brilliant storyteller. Dan did it all. And when the moment was big, he was at his best.” Tirico also took a moment to acknowledge Hicks’s wife Hannah Storm, and the relationship they built from newsroom beginnings. “But this isn’t just the story of a great sportscaster, it’s a love story too,” Tirico said. “With his equally as talented and wonderful wife Hannah, the greatest sportscasting couple of all time. A story that started on the anchor desk at CNN, continued to NBC, and was shared with so many of us for the last 32 years.” “When the moment was big, he was at his best.” Mike Tirico honors Dan Hicks as a talented professional, family man, and true friend. https://t.co/YV0AnyCCs3 — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 16, 2026 Later on in the broadcast, Tirico and his partner Cris Collinsworth spoke more about their relationship with Hicks. “This has been a tough weekend for all of us at NBC. Tough for us to work tonight, after the passing of a great friend in Dan Hicks,” Tirico said. “It’s been such a sad week for so many people at NBC obviously, us included,” Collinsworth, who called NFL games alongside Hicks decades ago, added. “But you can’t help but think how much joy and how much humor that man brought to all of us. He was such a professional, but when you were around him and he was doing his impersonations, he was just so much fun, and he is dearly, dearly missed.” “That picture you see is Danny. That smile,” Tirico said. “That smile was always on his face. When he worked with people, he made everybody he worked with better. He brought out the best in his coworkers.” Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth remember Dan Hicks on the NBC SNF broadcast. https://t.co/tHx49I6Kpp — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 16, 2026 While Hicks may no longer be with us, several of his calls on the biggest moments in sports will last beyond any of our lifetimes. The post Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth pay touching tribute to Dan Hicks appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Luka Doncic Caught On Camera Taking Clipboard Away From Lakers’ Coaching Staff In Viral Incident
item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - NOVEMBER 15: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers celebrates during the game against the Phoenix Suns on November 15, 2026 at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Barry Gossage/NBAE via Getty Images) Luka Doncic once again had a big night in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns tonight. He finished with 43 points, nine assists, and three rebounds, shooting 13-28 from the field (46.4% FG) and 5-13 from beyond the arc (38.4% 3P). The Lakers held a 31-point lead near the end of the third quarter, but the Suns cut it to five points down the stretch as they made a late push to compete. In a viral incident during the fourth quarter, the broadcast caught Luka Doncic taking the clipboard away from JJ Redick and his coaching staff to draw up the team’s play to close out the game. Luka took coaching into his own hands 😳 — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 15, 2026 NBA fans saw this unusual moment on social media and flooded it with mixed reactions to Luka Doncic taking over from the coaches to close out tonight’s win. Some appreciated his leadership initiative, while others saw it as a sign of disrespect. “Don’t complain. People have been wanting Luka to show leadership of ‘his’ team, so here you go.” “Luka said, ‘Forget the coach, I’ve got this.’ 😭😂” “I don’t like him snatching that out of her hands.” “His team blew a 31-point lead; I don’t blame him.” “You can do this when you’re a court assassin like him.” “Even Kobe wasn’t this disrespectful… lol.” Several similar reactions flooded social media as the Lakers eventually held on to the lead and won by eight points. After the game, the Lakers’ media asked Luka Doncic about the incident at the press conference. “That stays between the team, man. That’ll stay with the team; they know what I was communicating,” Doncic said as he refused to reveal the details of the incident. So it remains unknown why Luka Doncic did this down the stretch, but it clearly shows he knows that even when defense isn’t his primary responsibility, the leadership onus is on him to rally the troops. In my opinion, this is not a sign of disrespect. Even LeBron James has done something similar to this in the past when he was the face of the Lakers. The team has improved to 12-2 and extended their winning streak to eight games, with Luka Doncic dropping MVP-caliber performances every other night. He is currently averaging 39.0 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 7.8 assists while shooting 48.6% from the field and 40.6% from beyond the arc. The Lakers now move to face the Hornets at Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday night, November 17. It remains to be seen how long this winning streak lasts with Doncic in such fiery form and leading the Lakers from the front.

item.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza states the obvious about his tough start vs. Seahawks
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza states the obvious about his tough start vs. Seahawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Fernando Mendoza made the first start of his NFL career against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10, and it did not go great. The rookie Las Vegas Raiders quarterback got on the board early with a rushing touchdown , but he struggled in the passing game (17-of-29, 143 yards, no touchdowns) as the Raiders fell, 21-13. The No. 1 overall pick in this year’s draft acknowledges that his challenging performance against the reigning Super Bowl champions is the first step in a long learning process for him as an NFL quarterback . “There’s a lot of things I need to improve on out on that field,” Mendoza said, per Jesse Merrick. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) One such area of improvement Mendoza cited is his pocket presence, stating that he needs to be “more composed.” Mendoza was sacked six times by the Seahawks in his debut start, which was not entirely on the Raiders’ offensive line. The team’s previous starter, Kirk Cousins, had been sacked just 11 times in his nine starts for Las Vegas this season. Mendoza must do a better job of feeling the pressure inside the pocket, when to scramble, and when to throw balls away. That will usually come with more experience. However, the Raiders could also stand to help out their rookie quarterback by giving him a more reliable offensive weapons. The Raiders’ RB tandem of Mike Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty had a disappointing performance, combining for just 41 yards on 17 carries. Meanwhile, tight end Brock Bowers left the game early due to an ankle injury , further limiting Mendoza’s receiving options. Mendoza and the Raiders will look to make some improvements next week, when they take on the Denver Broncos fresh off their bye week. item.title: 'Time is running out.' How Texans fumbled a golden opportunity to get back into the playoff race.
item.description: Emari Demercado, Tank Dell and the Texans' offense struggled mightily after jumping out to a 17-point lead and departed Cleveland with a crushing loss to the Browns that could be a significant hit to their playof hopes. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) CLEVELAND - The Houston Texans held a 3-point lead with 5:19 remaining when safety Calen Bullock intercepted Clevleand Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson at Houston's 23-yard-line. It should have been a moment of victory for the Texans, who for one half, played better than the Browns. The Texans should have been able to run out the clock on offense. On defense, they should have been able to stop the Browns. But things have rarely gone as planned for the Texans this season. They lost to their own former franchise quarterback Watson and the Browns 27-24, falling to 3-6 on Sunday at Huntington Bank Field. And again, the Texans allowed another team to score a game-winning touchdown against them in the game's final minutes. If this sounds like a broken record, it's because it is one. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The Texans are the only team in the past 50 seasons to lose five times within their first nine games when tied or leading in the final two minutes. "It goes back to the fact that we can't hurt ourselves," coach DeMeco Ryans said. item.title: #13 St. Johns 79, Syracuse 62: tough second half derails Orange in Madison Square Garden
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 15: Kiyan Anthony #7 of the Syracuse Orange looks on during the first half against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images NEW YORK — For the first time since 2015, Sunday night showcased Syracuse and St. John’s facing off at Madison Square Garden in New York City, and after a promising start for the Orange, at the end of the day this matchup showed there are still some growing pains that Coach McNamara’s squad need to fight through. Especially against a nationally ranked opponent as St. John’s outscored Syracuse 49-29 in the second half in route to a 79-62 victory. But while it feels crazy that the two in-state rivals have not played in “World’s Most Famous Arena” in so long, it is safe to say the game lived up to the hype right from the jump. With a Garden at least 60% filled with fans in dressed in Orange, those rooting for the ’Cuse all erupted early. Ryan Moesch got a mismatch on a pick and roll with center Rueben Prey guarding him. And safe to say he took advantage, breaking the junior’s ankles and burying a wide open triple to give Syracuse an 8-6 lead at the first media timeout. But the real story of the first half was Kiyan Anthony. It was the sophomore’s first game at MSG, and he came off the bench leading the Orange with 10 points, getting to the charity stripe on three and-1 opportunities and converting on two of them. Crazy enough, Kiyan one of the main reasons Syracuse took a 33-30 lead into halftime against the naiton’s 13th ranked team. But for the second consecutive game, Syracuse came out flat in the second half, surrendering an 16-2 run to their opponent and quickly giving up the lead they worked so hard to earn in the first 20 minutes. All of a sudden it was 46-35 Red Storm before you could even blink. Until a bit of a response off the bench from Amari Monroe, who went on a quick 5-0 run on his own and cut the deficit to six at 46-40. However, the Pitino press was grueling, and suffocated the Orange right when you thought they might get back into the game. Syracuse could not buy a basket in the second half, shooting 33% from the field and only scoring a mere 29 points. The Orange showed a bit of fight late, but they could never make the big shot to really make the Red Storm feel any pressure while also turning the ball over at very inopportune times.

item.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake freshman Taylor Loria moves the ball for Burnt Hills during Sunday's Class B state championship game at Arlington High School in LaGrangeville. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) LAGRANGEVILLE - Winning a state championship is extremely difficult to do. Lakeland (21-2-1 overall) standout Gianna Santini, a UMass Lowell field hockey commit, finally found the back of the cage as she converted on a penalty corner for the Hornets early in the second overtime period. "Sharon Sarsen is a phenomenal coach and has a phenomenal program," Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake head coach Kelly Vrooman said of Lakeland. "She's been there for years and they're a well-oiled machine. I knew this coming into it, and our girls didn't take them lightly. We both have young teams and I just think we fell a little short." Lakeland's win at Arlington High School gave the program its 14th state title, which have all come under Sarsen, with the first coming in 1990. For the most part, Sunday night’s game answered those doubts. Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks in scoring with 18 points, adding five rebounds on an efficient 8-9 shooting from the field to go with it in 27 minutes of action. Although he ended the game with a +/- rating of -14, one could safely say that he was one of the better players for Dallas. In all fairness, it is hard to say Risacher was impactful simply because of how the Celtics put the game away in the first half itself. Still, with a quick six points in the second quarter and another seven points in the third, the former first-round pick helped Dallas stabilize their offense, ensuring that they remained marginally competitive for the remainder of the game. This season, Risacher is averaging 8.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 42.4% from the field. Although his production seems to be down compared to last season, the 21-year-old is gradually adapting to his new role in Dallas. Dallas Desperately Needs Dereck Lively II Back Aside from all the factors that stood out from Sunday night’s game, the most important one was probably the need for a stronger interior presence. While Dallas typically benefits from a strong big man rotation featuring Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse , Dereck Lively II’s absence was telling against the Celtics. Dallas’ centers were completely outmatched against Boston. Gafford, who has cultivated a reputation for being a phenomenal blue-collar big man, posted only three points and four rebounds against the Celtics. Off the bench, Cisse, who gave the Mavericks much to be optimistic about last season, had virtually no opportunities to contribute, notching only one point and a rebound in four minutes of playing time. With the Celtics beating the Mavericks on the rebounding glass 52-38 and also outscoring them 36-32 in the paint, Dallas clearly needs a stronger presence on the inside. In this regard, the Mavericks can only hope Dereck Lively II returns to action soon. Given the 22-year-old’s rebounding and elite rim protection ability, Dallas would benefit greatly from having another reliable center in their frontcourt rotation.

item.title: Evan McPherson's Bengals-record field-goal streak ends at 25
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson's team-record streak of consecutive field goals made ended at 25, with a miss on a 43-yard attempt during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. It was McPherson's first field-goal miss of the season. McPherson made a 24-yarder in the first quarter. McPherson made a pair of field goals, including one from 57 yards, during the Bengals' NFL Week 9 win against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. McPherson made a 26-yard field goal to break the franchise record for most consecutive field goals converted with 22, during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 5 win against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. McPherson's streak dated back to Week 11 of the 2025 season. He broke the record held by Shayne Graham, who made 21 consecutive FGs in 2007. McPherson was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September. McPherson converted each of his eight field-goal attempts and eight extra points over the Bengals' three games in September. McPherson 's 32 points scored in September tied for the most by any NFL kicker, while his FG total tied for the most by an AFC kicker. McPherson also led all kickers in FGs made from 50 or more yards (five). McPherson is in his sixth NFL season, all with the Bengals. In 2025, McPherson broke his own record for longest field goal in team history with a 63-yarder to end the first half of the Week 12 loss to New England at Paycor Stadium. McPherson's kick was one of 14 field goals in NFL history of at least 63 yards. McPherson attempted a 67-yard field goal at the end of the first half of the team's NFL Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. He made the attempt , but it didn't count. The Packers called timeout, and the whistle blew to negate what would have been an NFL record. McPherson played in 12 games during the 2024 season , missing time because of a groin injury. item.title: Rams make history with absurd Ronnie Rivers spamming to finish off the Cardinals
item.description: Arianna Grainey-Imagn Images Rams make history with absurd Ronnie Rivers spamming to finish off the Cardinals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams leaned heavily into Puka Nacua and Matthew Stafford in the past. But LA and Sean McVay turned to a surprise option to wear down the Arizona Cardinals: Ronnie Rivers. The undrafted running back out of Fresno State stole the spotlight late in the 34-6 rout down in Glendale, Arizona. And LA made history in the process with Rivers, per ESPN Insights after the game . “The Rams ended their victory with a 17-play drive that took the final 12:15 of the game. The first 15 plays were all carries by Ronnie Rivers. Rivers is the first player with 15+ touches on a single drive over the last 25 seasons, previous most in that span was 13,” the account posted on X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rivers’ best run became a 16-yarder. He also delivered an 11-yard scamper during that drive. But he emerged as the stunning third trusted backfield option on a team featuring two backfield stars. Ram fans are used to Kyren Williams wearing down defenses and becoming a Pro Bowler in the process. But Williams settled for 12 carries for 23 yards and averaged 1.9 yards a carry. Blake Corum pummeled Arizona the most, racking up 17 carries for 100 yards. Rivers, though, handed the Rams 81 rushing yards which becomes a career-high for him. He averaged 5.4 yards per carry in the desert. Los Angeles once landed him after the 2022 NFL Draft, but he never began his career with the Rams. Arizona rose as his first NFL employer, taking him after that draft class. So Sunday became long-awaited closet revenge on the first team that released him. And he pulled it off amid injuries to Nacua and Rivers’ fellow Fresno State grad Davante Adams . Related: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA? (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell to 1-8 earlier today after coming up just short of beating the Indianapolis Colts, 24-22. Miami’s offense played well enough under quarterback Kyle McCord, making his NFL debut after spending his rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad last year, and the defense did its part to keep Miami in the game. The special teams let down the Dolphins – with kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point during the game. The Dolphins’ loss was yet another straight-up loss, but they did enough to cover the 3.5-point spread throughout the week, or the 4.5-point mark to which the spread ballooned on Sunday. Miami is being given an even bigger window for next week’s game. Miami visits the Buffalo Bills in Week 11, the first of two meetings between the AFC East rivals in 2026. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Dolphins have little chance against the division-leading Bills. The opening line has the Bills favored by 16.5 points . Buffalo demolished the New York Jets, another AFC East division opponent, on Sunday, 31-12. The win moved the Bills to 8-1 for the year and keeps them in the top spot in the AFC playoff picture, a game ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs and Jacksonville Jaguars. The winner of tonight’s Sunday Night Football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will also reach the 7-2 mark, a game behind Buffalo. The Bills are -1800 on the moneyline for the straight-up victory, while the Dolphins are +980. The point total opened at 47.5. McCord will start his second game in Week 11, looking to continue to grow in the Dolphins’ offense as he replaces Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve with a groin injury. McCord finished the game 17-for-32 for 209 yards with no touchdown passes or interceptions; he did score a rushing touchdown. item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch. Continue reading...

item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
item.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
